title: VPC Onboarding: Decision Journal & Meeting Minute Template
content:
Purpose:
This document is a lightweight, standardized decision journal and meeting minute template to use during customer VPC onboarding, network approval reviews, and evidence handoffs. The goal is to produce concise, auditable records that feed into the customer-facing handover bundle and Redwood’s internal audit logs without duplicating effort.

Scope:
- Applies to VPC/private-deployments onboarding interactions that require an approval gate, operator action, or audit evidence capture.
- Intended for use by product owners, operator engineers, solutions engineers, and SREs.
- Not a substitute for the long-form PRD; this is a working record for decisions, timeboxed approvals, and minute capture.

Why this exists (short):
Onboarding calls and approval meetings are the primary place where trade-offs are made (eg: ephemeral NAT vs. customer-managed NAT, readonly telemetry forwarders, retention windows). Those decisions need to be (a) captured in a consistent format for audits, (b) surfaced into the evidence bundle we hand to the customer, and (c) tied to follow-up actions with owners and SLAs. Too often we have fragmented notes across Slack/Jira/Confluence — this template centralizes the transactional record.

How to use this template (quick):
1. Create a new doc from this template before the onboarding call and pre-fill meeting metadata and known artifacts.
2. During the call, a scribe captures decisions using the Decision Log table below and records immediate action items in the Minutes section.
3. After the call, owner(s) confirm the record within 48 hours; a confirmed record becomes the canonical onboarding artifact to include in the customer evidence package and in attachment to any approval gate ticket.

Decision Journal (structured entries) - REQUIRED FORMAT:
- Entry ID: DJ-YYYYMMDD-N (unique; e.g., DJ-20250211-1)
- Date/time: 2025-02-11 14:20 UTC
- Participants: list (role - name; ex: operator - Miguel Torres)
- Decision summary (1-2 sentences): concise decision statement
- Rationale: bulleted reasons, risks, and alternatives considered (include approximate cost/latency delta if known)
- Evidence referenced: list of artifacts (log excerpts, egress policy snapshots, sample attestation tokens) — include file names or links to attachments
- Approval level: auto-approvable / operator-approved / customer-approved / executive-approval-required
- Timebox: the duration this decision is valid for (e.g., temporary: 30 days; permanent; review in 6 months)
- Owner(s): Who must act on operationalization or follow-up (name + email)
- Audit tag(s): short tags for indexing (eg: telemetry-retention, nat-choice, fallback-route)
- Status: proposed | accepted | superseded | revoked

Minute Template (use during meeting) - fill fields below:
- Meeting title:
- Meeting id / link (calendar):
- Date/time (UTC):
- Organizer: (team / person)
- Scribe: (person capturing minutes)
- Participants (role - name - company):
- Objective: (1-2 lines)
- Agenda bullets:
  - 1) Network topology review
  - 2) Audit/evidence retention requirements
  - 3) Approval gates and roles
  - 4) Rollout plan and rollback criteria
  - 5) Action items / owners
- Key decisions (reference Decision Journal entry IDs):
  - DJ-... : (one-line summary)
- Open questions (explicit, with owner and due date):
- Action items (owner / due / success criteria):
- Links & attachments captured during call: (list)
- Next meeting (if any):

Evidence checklist to attach to onboarding bundle (minimal):
- Network snapshot (customer-provided CIDR, peering config) - file: cust-vpc-snapshot.json (required)
- Approval artifact (signed assertion or ticket link) - e.g., jira://PD-812/approve (required)
- Operator attestation note (operator name + timestamp + hash) - attach small signed note 
- Sample telemetry forwarder config and retention settings (if telemetry enabled) - yaml
- Egress / firewall policy excerpt showing allowed destinations - text or screenshot
- Rollback plan checklist (how we will revert changes) - short steps
- Retention policy statement (where logs live, retention length, S3/ARC path)

Retention & Audit visibility guidance (recommended):
- Decision journal entries with status=accepted must be retained in Redwood internal logs for at least 3 years.
- Evidence bundle (attachments + network snapshot) must be archived in the customer’s handover bucket and a copy kept in Redwood’s secure evidence store for 1 year by default (longer for enterprise customers per contract).
- For timeboxed decisions (e.g., temporary operator overrides) set explicit review dates; create a reminder/cron job and a Jira follow-up ticket assigned to the Owner.

Approval-level decision patterns (suggested defaults):
- Auto-approvable: low-risk telemetry config changes, retention length <= 7 days, no egress changes
- Operator-approved: changes that affect operator-side routing or require operator scripts (eg: NAT translation changes)
- Customer-approved: any change that modifies customer-managed firewall, peering, or access to customer resources
- Executive approval: policy exceptions that affect SLAs or legal commitments (rare)

Escalation & rollback hooks:
- If an implemented decision causes degraded latency > 50th percentile SLO for 15 minutes post-change, trigger immediate rollback and notify Incident channel + customer success.
- For failed handover (evidence mismatch), escalate to Product lead and attach Decision Journal entries to the escalation Jira ticket.

Sample Decision Journal entry (example):
- Entry ID: DJ-20250211-1
- Date/time: 2025-02-11 14:20 UTC
- Participants: operator - Miguel Torres; solutions - Aisha Patel; cust - DevOps (Acme Inc: Priya Sharma)
- Decision summary: Allow Redwood-managed telemetry forwarder to send anonymized metered metrics to redwood-telemetry-prod over TLS port 443 behind the customer NAT.
- Rationale:
  - preserves low-latency metric shipping for debugging
  - reduces operator overhead vs. customer-managed forwarder by estimated 12% total ops cost
  - risk: customer requires PII-free telemetry; we will sample and redact at SDK level
- Evidence referenced: sample-forwarder-config-v1.yaml; runtime-sampling-proof.txt (hash: abc123)
- Approval level: customer-approved
- Timebox: review in 90 days
- Owner(s): solutions - Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Audit tags: telemetry-retention, telemetry-approval
- Status: accepted

Operational checklist after a decision is accepted (short):
- Create Jira follow-up ticket and link DJ entry ID
- Attach required evidence files to the ticket and to the customer handover bucket
- Add a reminder to the onboarding calendar for the review timebox
- If operator-run deployment required, include operator runbook snippet and runbook owner

Notes to self / implementation quirks (informal):
- Keep the Decision ID small and machine-sortable (DJ-YYYYMMDD-N); we can build a light parser later to index by tag and owner.
- Don’t overpopulate the Evidence bundle; prefer 3–5 decisive artifacts rather than huge log dumps.
- If customer refuses to provide network snapshot, escalate: we cannot proceed with auto-operator NAT changes without the snapshot.

Unresolved questions (for product discussion):
- Should Decision Journal entries auto-emit an immutable audit hash to our evidence store? Pros: tamper-evident. Cons: adds complexity to small onboarding flows.
- What is the minimal SLA for confirming a scribed meeting record? 24 hours feels tight; 48 hours is the current working assumption.

Related artifacts and references:
- Confluence onboarding playbook: confluence://private-deployments/vpc-onboarding-playbook
- Ticket for approval flow prototype: jira://PD-812
- Slack thread where this template was prototyped: slack://channel/private-deployments (thread ts:1623456789.000200)

Small checklist before closing a call (quick):
- Did we create a Decision Journal entry for each named decision? (Y/N)
- Are all Owner fields filled and agreed? (Y/N)
- Did we attach at least one evidence artifact per accepted decision? (Y/N)
- Did we create follow-up Jira tasks for timeboxed reviews? (Y/N)

Endnotes:
This template is intentionally lightweight — the product team expects iterations. Please copy this file to create a meeting-specific copy and append DJ entries as new lines. If you run into repeated manual bookkeeping (eg many handoffs per customer), flag PD-ops for automation work.

-- Jordan Lee (template author)
